items.title: 自由曾在此
items.text:
ASJ 英东物理社 · 数字纪念馆 · ARCHIVE NO. 001 — ∞

一座关于热爱的纪念馆

社团已成为过去。 那些提问、尝试与并肩的时刻，仍然属于我们。

留给过去，也留给以后。

items.title: 物理之外，是自由探索的我们
items.text:
ASJ 英东物理社曾希望创造一个平台：让学生用自己的方式理解物理、表达物理、实践物理。

这里收藏了它留下的讲稿、活动方案、设计与影像。社团已经不复存在，但那些认真做过的事，值得被记住。

items.title: 记述原则
items.text:
留存的材料并不完整：有的日期只写到月份，有的活动只有一句提及， 有的制度留在草案阶段。面对这些缺口，本站的取舍是：

  • 不补写未知的原因、日期与结果；材料到哪一步，正文就写到哪一步；
  • 材料之间口径不一致时并列保留各版本，不推定最终执行结果；
  • 过期目录中的草案仅作草案存档；
  • 全站一律用通行简体，包括引文、人名与组名。原始件多为繁体， 本站按字形转写，不改用字、标点与语序；选用繁体或英文的读者各得其所。

items.title: 阅读指引
items.text:
本站不向任何第三方发请求。 字体、样式与脚本全部自托管，图片点开是站内的查看器， 不会跳到别的域名。页脚的「数据隐私」写着同样的话。

首页的几段展陈用键盘也能走完：

  • Left Right —— 在「影像序章」的三幕之间切换，或翻动「一页，一页，留下来」
  • Home End —— 直接跳到第一幕或最后一幕
  • Esc —— 关掉放大的原件

系统里如果开了「减少动态效果」，滚动吸附与进出动画会自动关掉， 展陈改为静态排布，内容一样是全的。

items.title: 不是所有故事，都有一个郑重的句点
items.text:
有些事停下了，留下的是几份文件、一些照片、还没来得及讲完的想法。

这个网站把它们放在一起。让曾经参与的人有一个可以回来的地方，也让后来经过的人知道：这里曾有一群人，认真地想过，试过，一起做过。

「自由曾在此」是这座纪念馆的名字。它纪念提问的自由、探索的热情，以及人与人之间真实发生过的联结。

谨以此页，致所有成员、老师、参与者，以及那些未被记录下来的帮助。

items.text:

  • 逐页保留原貌，包括其中尚未落地的内容；
  • 材料之间口径不一致时并列保留各版本，不推定哪一版最终执行；

资料出处

社牌是一套参数化设计工程，不只是几张图。原始工程见 社牌设计工程：

  • source/物理社工牌设计全部模板.svgz —— 全部模板的源工程

items.title: 第 2 页 · 关于 ASJ 英东物理社团
items.text:
关于 / About

ASJ Physics Club 的诞生，并非只为了解题， 也不是为了增加课外活动的数量，而是希望创造一个 让学生用自己的方式理解物理、表达物理、实践物理的平台。

本页的地位

这是整套材料中唯一一处对社团宗旨的正面定义， 也是后续「理解物理、表达物理、实践物理」这一表述的源头。 该表述在开场口语稿、招新宣讲稿中被反复引用。

「不是……也不是……而是……」的三段句式，明确排除了两种定位： 解题训练与课外活动数量。

items.title: 第 5 页 · 会费收集说明
items.text:
会费收集说明 / Membership Fee Collection Instructions

为了更好地支持本学期及以后的物理社团活动的开展， 本学期将设置社团会费自愿缴纳机制。

特别说明的是：本次会费缴纳完全遵循自愿原则。 缴纳会费并不是加入社团的前提，不缴纳也不会影响同学参与社团日常活动。

In order to better support the development of the physics club activities this term, a voluntary membership fee payment system will be implemented this term.

It should be noted specifically: This fee payment is entirely based on a voluntary principle. Paying the fee is not a prerequisite for joining the club; failure to pay will not affect students' participation in the club's daily activities.

自愿原则的三重表述

本页用「自愿缴纳机制」「完全遵循自愿原则」「不缴纳也不会影响」 三重表述界定同一件事，措辞强度递增。 这是留存材料中对会费问题最谨慎的一页。

具体用途与使用原则另见 会费使用说明， 制度设计见 会费与贡献积分制度。

items.title: 第 7 页 · 关于招新
items.text:
关于招新 / Regarding the recruitment of new members

新学期，物理社团正式开启招新。如果你对物理有兴趣，如果你喜欢思考、喜欢探索、 喜欢动手，如果你曾经被某一个实验、某一个现象、某一个问题点燃过好奇心， 那么欢迎你加入我们。

你不需要一开始就「很厉害」，也不需要已经学会很多超纲知识。 真正重要的是，你愿不愿意保持好奇，愿不愿意去问一个「为什么」， 愿不愿意在看似普通的世界里，发现那些不普通的规律。

招新的门槛表述

本页明确取消知识门槛（「不需要很厉害」「不需要超纲知识」）， 把筛选标准转为意愿（好奇 / 追问 / 发现）。 这一表述与 第 2 页 的社团宗旨直接呼应。

items.title: 第 6 页 · 制度说明首页
items.text:
物理社社费与贡献积分制度说明 社费 · 贡献积分 · 公开监督 · 合规边界

核心立场 - 让社团活动更稳定 - 让资金和规则更透明 - 让制度边界更清晰

四项原则：

原则 说明 公开透明 收入来源、支出用途、凭证与余额可查 自愿参与 缴纳会费不是加入社团的前提 合规运行 社费与积分不越界，不做货币化设计 社团自治 由社内会计与出纳监管，规则提前公布

依据：社费草案、法律条文与定义、稳定／代币风险建议文档

「依据」三份文件

本页明确列出了制度设计所依据的三份文件： 《社费草案》《法律条文与定义》《稳定／代币风险建议文档》。

这三份文件即 资料/ 中的 功勋制度草案、法律条文与定义、稳定 · 讨论材料。 按 白皮书与留存边界 的公开范围，本站不公开其内容。

items.title: 第 7 页 · 为什么需要这套制度
items.text:
为什么需要这套制度

制度不是为了「收费」，而是为了解决社团活动运行中的现实问题。

# 问题 具体表现 1 报销时间差 学校正式审批和报销需要流程；器材与材料常常需要提前采购；社团需要具备短期垫付能力 2 活动支出多样 实验、竞赛、例会和福利活动都会产生费用；部分支出可能不属于统一报销范围；需要清楚区分资金用途 3 信任与规则 社费和积分若规则不清，容易引发误解；账目不透明会造成信任危机；提前建立规则能减少纠纷

用制度化方式保障活动持续开展，而不是用临时办法解决每一次支出。

本页的论证结构

本页用「三个现实问题 → 一个对比结论」的结构论证制度必要性。 其中「报销时间差 / 短期垫付能力」是最具体的一条： 它解释了为什么社团需要持有现金，而不只是记账。

items.title: 第 8 页 · 社费资金池设计
items.text:
社费资金池设计 将经费用途分清楚，是后续公开监督和风险控制的基础。

固定资金池

  • 用于垫付可报销的社团支出
  • 帮助应对学校审批前的时间差
  • 强调凭证留存与后续核销
  • 不应被设计为个人收益来源

活动资金池

  • 用于承担部分不可报销活动费用
  • 如小型材料、活动组织和福利安排
  • 支出应与社团活动直接相关
  • 金额、用途和审批流程需公开

建议原则：社费自愿、用途明确、凭证齐全、定期公示。

「活动资金池」与「流动资金池」的命名差异

本页第二个池子名为「活动资金池」； 而 物理社功勋系统资金流转白皮书 与 会员公开白皮书 中名为 「流动资金池」，且定义为「进入会员个人账户、可用于社团内部活动和资源使用的部分」。

两者职责描述接近但不等同：本页强调「不可报销费用」， 白皮书强调「计入个人账户」。并列保留。

items.title: 第 9 页 · 贡献积分的定位
items.text:
贡献积分的定位 积分可以记录贡献，但绝不能被包装成货币、投资或收益凭证。

它应该是 它不应该是 ✓ 社团内部贡献记录 ✕ 货币、代币或通证 ✓ 活动参与激励工具 ✕ 投资或融资工具 ✓ 福利活动权益记录 ✕ 固定收益或分红承诺 ✓ 社团自治辅助机制 ✕ 可转让、交易、折现的凭证

本页是整套制度的合规底线

右侧四条的措辞（「绝不能被包装成」）是本套演示文稿中语气最强的一页。 它把积分与「货币 / 投资 / 收益凭证」三类事物做了切割， 与 法律条文与定义 中对代币发行融资与非法集资「四性」的分析互为对应。

items.title: 第 10 页 · 积分如何获得与使用
items.text:
积分如何获得与使用 积分应围绕真实贡献产生，规则必须提前公布。

来源 举例 参与 例会听讲、参与实验、参加社团活动 贡献 讲解题目、协助组织、完成社团任务 表现 竞赛获奖、大型活动突出贡献 记录 形成公开规则下的贡献积分

使用边界 - 仅限社团内部福利活动或权益记录 - 不得转让、交易、折现或承诺经济回报 - 不得用积分制造「投入越多收益越高」的预期

「不得制造预期」

第三条边界是本页最特殊的一条：它限制的不是行为，而是预期的形成。 这与第 9 页「不是投资工具」在逻辑上互补。

items.title: 第 11 页 · 争议处理机制
items.text:
争议处理机制 规则越清晰，越能保护社员、社团干部和指导老师。

四步流程：

步骤 动作 1 提交申请 社员提出书面申请并说明原因 2 审核记录 按制度审核，留存时间、金额和依据 3 结果回馈 告知处理结果，必要时公示规则依据 4 申诉说明 成员可提出异议、补充说明或申请复核

器材损坏处理

  • 应依据事实、证据和章程条款处理
  • 不建议用简单扣积分替代正式赔偿
  • 应保留说明、协商和申诉空间

避免霸道条款

  • 减少「最终解释权归社团所有」的单向表达
  • 改为「按章程解释，接受监督与申诉」
  • 处理结果应可追溯、可说明

本页值得单独指出的一点

「避免霸道条款」这一小节主动限制社团自身的权力， 并要求以「按章程解释，接受监督与申诉」替代「最终解释权归社团所有」。 这在学生社团的制度文本中并不常见。

items.title: 第 12 页 · 公开账本与知情权
items.text:
公开账本与知情权 透明不是负担，而是减少误会和保护社团干部的机制。

层次 内容 公开账本 凭证 · 流向 · 余额 整体收支 公开收入来源；公开支出用途；定期汇总公示 个人记录 本人社费记录；本人积分记录 原始凭证 支付截图；发票或收据；采购清单 监督机制 社员查询；老师指导；问题申诉

透明被论证为对干部的保护

副标题把「透明」定义为保护社团干部的机制，而不只是约束他们。 这一视角与常见的「透明是为了监督」不同。

items.title: 第 13 页 · 执行落地流程
items.text:
执行落地流程 建议先试行、再修订，避免制度一开始就过重或过急。

步骤 动作 1 公开草案 向社员与老师说明制度目的，集中收集意见 2 修订细则 明确社费、积分、监督和争议处理规则 3 建立账本 统一记录收支、凭证、个人记录和公示周期 4 定期复盘 每月或每学期检查执行效果并修订问题

「先试行、再修订」

本页明确了制度不是一次性定稿，而是把修订机制写进了流程本身（第 4 步）。 这与 功勋系统 后续出现 v1.0 → 正式版第一版 → 会员公开版的 多版本演进相印证。

items.title: 第 14 页 · 收束
items.text:
让制度服务社团建设

每一笔钱都花在明处， 每一份贡献都被公平记录。

首尾呼应

末页的两句话分别对应第 6 页四项原则中的公开透明（钱花在明处） 与第 9–10 页的积分定位（贡献被记录，但不被货币化）。

items.title: Freedom Was Here
items.text:
ASJ YINGDONG PHYSICS CLUB · DIGITAL MEMORIAL · ARCHIVE NO. 001 — ∞

A memorial to something that was loved

The club is in the past. The questions, the attempts, and the hours we stood side by side still belong to us.

Left to the past, and left for afterwards.

items.title: Beyond physics, there was us — exploring freely
items.text:
The ASJ Yingdong Physics Club set out to build a platform: a place for students to understand physics, express physics, and practise physics in their own way.

What it left behind is collected here — speech scripts, event plans, design work, and photographs. The club no longer exists, but the work that was done in earnest deserves to be remembered.

items.title: More than a name
items.text:
A club badge, one page of a speech, one attempt to hand an idea over to two hands. Freedom once had these concrete shapes.

How this site records things

This site records only the fragments that can be confirmed in the surviving material.

  • No attempt is made to fill in the unknown reason or date of the club's suspension;
  • Where the sources disagree on dates, each version is kept side by side; no final outcome is inferred;
  • Drafts in the expired design directory are archived as drafts only, and are not assumed to be the version actually issued.

See Thanks and Afterword · editorial notes.

items.title: Editorial principles
items.text:
The surviving material is not complete: some dates go no further than a month, some events are mentioned only in passing, and some rules never left the draft stage. Faced with those gaps, this site chooses:

  • not to write in unknown causes, dates or outcomes — where the material stops, the text stops;
  • where sources disagree, to preserve all versions side by side and presume none to be final;
  • to archive drafts as drafts when they come from an outdated directory;
  • to give everything in the conventional Simplified forms — quotations, personal and group names alike. Where the originals are in Traditional Chinese, this site transcribes the characters without altering the wording, the punctuation or the word order; readers who choose Traditional or English get their own tree.

items.title: Reading this site
items.text:
This site makes no request to any third party. Fonts, styles and scripts are all served from this site's own origin, and images open in an on-site viewer rather than another domain; the “Data & privacy” note in the footer says the same thing.

The exhibits on the home page can also be driven from the keyboard:

  • Left Right — move between the three scenes of the opening sequence, or turn the pages of “one page, one page, left behind”
  • Home End — jump to the first or the last scene
  • Esc — close an enlarged original

If your system has “reduce motion” turned on, scroll snapping and enter/exit animations switch themselves off and the exhibits fall back to a static layout — the content is all still there.

items.title: Matters that cannot be confirmed
items.text:
What this site does not fill in

  • The club's end date and reason — the material cannot confirm them, so this site does not fill them in.
  • The Flight Festival's final results — the surviving material contains only preparation files and blank forms (the results sheet and the sign-in sheet were both left unfilled), with no record of any actual result.
  • The number of competition entrants — the material can confirm an award rate of 100%, but no original record of the number of entrants was found.

items.title: Not every story gets a solemn full stop
items.text:
Some things stop, and what they leave behind is a few files, some photographs, and ideas there was no time to finish saying.

This website puts them together in one place. It gives those who once took part a place they can come back to, and lets those who pass by later know: there was once a group of people here who thought seriously, tried, and did things together.

“Freedom Was Here” is the name of this memorial. It commemorates the freedom to ask, the appetite to explore, and the connections that genuinely happened between people.

This page is offered to every member, teacher and participant, and to the help that was never recorded.

items.title: The three kinds of surviving originals
items.text:
Scripts, design files and photographs. They were not made for a memorial — they were left behind while the work was being done, and that is exactly why they preserve how things looked at the time: ideas that never landed, templates that were never used up, and photographs whose dates can only be pinned down to a month.

This part gathers three kinds of original material:

Section Contents Scale Photo Archive Photographs from the surviving material Ten frames Design Archive Emblem, badges, wayfinding signs, posters, cup design One parametric project Assembly Room Presentation decks from the three spring 2026 assemblies 31 pages, original order kept

items.title: Why they are kept in one section
items.text:
What the three have in common is that they are originals, not retellings.

So the same editorial line applies to all of them:

  • each page is kept as it was, including content that never landed;
  • where sources disagree, all versions are preserved side by side and none is presumed to be the final one;
  • drafts in an outdated directory are archived as drafts, not presumed to be what was actually issued.

Each page names its own 资料/ source at the top, so every item can be checked.

items.title: List of originals
items.text:
The materials directory Original on-site photographs holds 19 image files in total. The filenames keep their WeChat timestamps, so every single one has a verifiable exact time.

What these times mean

The timestamp in a WeChat filename records the moment the file was processed or saved by WeChat. It is usually close to the shooting time, but it is not the same as the shutter time. This site uses them to summarise the rough period in which activities took place, and does not use them to establish a precise moment of shooting.

items.title: On the correspondence between page photographs and originals
items.text:
The photographs on this site's pages are re-encoded versions1 of these originals.

Why the source file is not labelled for each one

Several photographs in the surviving material have exactly the same dimensions (for example 20260421123547, 20260421123548 and 20260421130606 are all 1280 × 853), and after re-encoding the correspondence cannot be determined uniquely from file attributes alone.

This site therefore does not label each page photograph with its original filename — giving a definite answer when the evidence is insufficient is worse than giving none.

items.title: 04.21 Assembly and recruitment · Page-by-page record
items.text:
SLIDES 1–12 · 2026.04.21 · FINAL

What this page is

This page transcribes all 12 pages of 21 April assembly deck (final), page by page. The deck is in Traditional Chinese; quotations are transcribed into simplified characters1, and the material between slides is added by this site. The English renderings are added by this site as well.

For the wider context see Assembly Scripts; for the minutes of the assembly see The first assembly and recruitment.

items.title: Slide 1 · 封面 (Cover)
items.text:
ASJ英東物理社集會暨招新活動 ASJ Yingdong Physics Club Gathering and Recruitment Event 2026/04/21

This was the club's first formal assembly this term, and it also served as recruitment. The Chinese–English bilingual title continues on every later page, forming the fixed layout of this deck.

items.title: Slide 2 · 關於 ASJ 英東物理社團 (About the ASJ Yingdong Physics Club)
items.text:
關於 / About

ASJ Physics Club 的誕生，並非只為了解題， 也不是為了增加課外活動的數量，而是希望創造一個 讓學生用自己的方式理解物理、表達物理、實踐物理的平臺。

English rendering.

About.

The ASJ Physics Club was born not only to solve problems, nor to add one more extracurricular activity, but to create a platform for students to understand physics, express physics and practise physics in their own way.

The standing of this page

This is the only place in all the surviving material where the club's purpose is defined directly, and the source of the later phrase “understand physics, express physics, practise physics”. That phrase is quoted again and again in the opening script and in the recruitment speech.

The three-part sentence “not… nor… but…” explicitly rules out two things the club was not: problem-solving drills and the number of extracurricular activities.

items.title: Slide 3 · 運營人員頒牌 (Officers receive their badges)
items.text:
運營人員頒牌 / Operational staff receive certificates

This slide lists the role, Chinese name and English name of all 14 officers:

Role Position Name English 社長 President 孔耀聰 Toby 副社長 Vice President 孫弘毅 Richard 學術負責 Academic Director 胡益成 Eric 活動指導 Event Director 陳詩潤 Mika 活動指導 Event Director 何蘇宇 Ryan 競賽指導 Competition Leader 楊弘毅 Daniel 競賽指導 Competition Leader 熊戀婷 Belinda 宣傳負責 PR 陸漢文 Kevin 宣傳負責 PR 韋皓顏 Yolanda 宣傳負責 PR 徐弘庭 Hugo 宣傳負責 PR 王悠然 Yoyo 組織運營 Operation Leader 肖子揚 Bernard 組織運營 Operation Leader 賴俊銘 Jimmy 組織運營 Operation Leader 嶽昀朗 Jason

The scope of “運營人員”

The 14 people on this slide are the club's officers; ordinary members are not included. The remaining members are listed in Governance and roster.

This list is identical character for character with Management roster (the fill variables used to batch-generate the club badges), so the two can be cross-checked.

items.title: Slide 4 · 教師社牌頒發儀式 (Presentation of the teachers' club badges)
items.text:
教師社牌頒發儀式 / Presentation of the Club Badge Ceremony

This slide lists all 6 advisors:

Role Name English 創社教師 / Founding Teacher 齊爾康 Sink 教師顧問 / Faculty Advisor 姚池 Icy 榮譽顧問 / Honorary Teacher Advisor 楊麗紅 Audrey 榮譽顧問 / Honorary Teacher Advisor 周曉鵬 Jason 榮譽顧問 / Honorary Teacher Advisor 奉海英 Yolanda 榮譽顧問 / Honorary Teacher Advisor 李佳佳 Cathy

One typo in the original files

Badge ceremony speech writes the faculty advisor as “姚弛”, while this slide and Management roster both have “姚池”. This site follows the majority of the original files.

items.title: Slide 5 · 會費收集說明 (Membership dues collection)
items.text:
會費收集說明 / Membership Fee Collection Instructions

為了更好地支持本學期及以後的物理社團活動的開展， 本學期將設置社團會費自願繳納機制。

特別說明的是：本次會費繳納完全遵循自願原則。 繳納會費並不是加入社團的前提，不繳納也不會影響同學參與社團日常活動。

In order to better support the development of the physics club activities this term, a voluntary membership fee payment system will be implemented this term.

It should be noted specifically: This fee payment is entirely based on a voluntary principle. Paying the fee is not a prerequisite for joining the club; failure to pay will not affect students' participation in the club's daily activities.

The voluntary principle stated three times

This slide defines the same thing three times over — “自願繳納機制”, “完全遵循自願原則”, “不繳納也不會影響” — with the wording growing stronger each time. It is the most cautious page in the surviving material on the question of dues.

The specific uses and the principles for spending them are set out in Notes on how dues were used; the system design is in Membership dues and contribution credits.

items.title: Slide 6 · 關於科技節紙飛機說明 (About the paper planes at the Science and Technology Festival)
items.text:
關於科技節紙飛機說明 / Explanation of Paper Airplanes for the Science and Technology Festival

以紙為帆，航跡英東

時間：4月30日 14：00 到 16:30

English rendering.

Explanation of Paper Airplanes for the Science and Technology Festival.

With paper as the sail, the journey reaches as far as the east.

Time: 30 April, 14:00 to 16:30.

With paper as the sail, the journey reaches as far as the east.

This slide lists three slots:

Time Segment 14:00–15:15 Folding for everyone · free flight 14:30–15:30 School-wide guessing game 15:30–17:00 The official flight competition

Times conflict within this page and between pages

  • Within the page: the heading says 14:00–16:30, but the last slot runs to 17:00, half an hour later than the heading;
  • Between pages: 27 April assembly deck moves the activity to 15:20–16:20; the poster draft says 15:00–16:10; the run-of-show document schedules it across a whole day.

All four versions are kept side by side; this site does not infer which time was finally used. For the full comparison see Sources · conflicting statements of time.

items.title: Slide 7 · 關於招新 (About recruitment)
items.text:
關於招新 / Regarding the recruitment of new members

新學期，物理社團正式開啟招新。如果你對物理有興趣，如果你喜歡思考、喜歡探索、 喜歡動手，如果你曾經被某一個實驗、某一個現象、某一個問題點燃過好奇心， 那麼歡迎你加入我們。

你不需要一開始就「很厲害」，也不需要已經學會很多超綱知識。 真正重要的是，你願不願意保持好奇，願不願意去問一個「為什麼」， 願不願意在看似普通的世界裏，發現那些不普通的規律。

English rendering.

Regarding the recruitment of new members.

In the new term, the physics club formally opens recruitment. If you are interested in physics, if you like to think, like to explore, like to work with your hands, if some experiment, some phenomenon, some question has ever caught your curiosity, then you are welcome to join us.

You do not have to be “very good” from the start, and you do not need to have learned a great deal beyond the syllabus. What really matters is whether you are willing to stay curious, willing to ask “why”, willing to find the uncommon laws in a world that looks ordinary.

How the threshold for recruitment is put

This slide explicitly removes the knowledge threshold (“you do not have to be very good”, “no knowledge beyond the syllabus”), and turns the test into a matter of willingness (curiosity / asking further / noticing). The wording answers directly to the club's purpose on slide 2.

items.title: Slide 8 · 活動照片 (Event photographs)
items.text:
活動照片

物理不是少數人的舞臺。它屬於願意認真思考、願意反復推敲、願意把問題真正想透的人。

2026 春季學期，讓我們帶著清晰的目標與更高的標準，再次出發。期待今年，我們再創佳績。

歡迎 ASJ英東物理社招新內容

來自「雞蛋撞地球」

English rendering.

Event photographs.

Physics is not a stage for a chosen few. It belongs to those who are willing to think carefully, to weigh a question over and over, and to think it through to the end.

In the spring term of 2026, let us set out again with clear goals and a higher standard. We look forward to doing well again this year.

Welcome ASJ Yingdong Physics Club recruitment material

From “Egg Drop”.

What this slide actually contains

This slide uses photographs of “雞蛋撞地球” (“Egg Drop”) as its recruitment image, captioned “Physics is not a stage for a chosen few”.

“Egg Drop” is the only activity in the surviving material with no plan and no date of its own; it is mentioned only on this slide and in Recruitment talk script. See Egg Drop.

items.title: Slide 9 · 自媒體部門說明 (The social media department)
items.text:
招募方向 拍攝、剪輯、策劃、文案、封面設計、運營

運轉方式 盈利前由 Sink 每月注入 1000 元專項經費

部門目標 讓熱愛被看見，讓內容產生價值，讓社團擁有自己的未來

適用場景 公眾號推文 / 招新發佈 / 集會宣講配套文案

讓熱愛被看見 · 讓內容產生價值 · 讓社團擁有自己的未來

English rendering.

What we are looking for — filming, editing, planning, copywriting, cover design, operations.

How it runs — before it makes a profit, Sink puts in 1000 yuan a month as dedicated funding.

What the department aims at — let what we love be seen, let the content have value, let the club have a future of its own.

Where it applies — the club's WeChat account posts / recruitment announcements / supporting copy for assembly talks.

Let what we love be seen · let the content have value · let the club have a future of its own.

What we value more is: whether you are willing to do something seriously, whether you are willing to take on responsibilities within the team, and whether you are willing to turn your interests into real abilities.

What this slide is

This is the social media department's founding statement, with four elements: what it recruits for, how it runs, what the department aims at, and where it applies. The line “before it turns a profit, Sink puts in a dedicated 1000 yuan a month” was announced publicly at the assembly, and is the only record of a funding source in the surviving material.

items.title: Slide 10 · 物理競賽成果展示 (Physics competition results)
items.text:
物理競賽成果展示

獲獎率 100% 金獎得獎率（四捨五入）90%

English rendering.

Physics competition results.

Award rate 100%; gold award rate (rounded) 90%.

How this slide differs from the recruitment speech

Recruitment talk script says “85% won gold”; this final slide says “90% (rounded)”.

The two differ by 5 percentage points, and this site keeps both side by side. For the conclusion and the sources see Physics competition · 100% award rate.

This is the only slide in the deck built around numbers, carrying two figures and no embellishment.

items.title: Slide 11 · Q&A
items.text:
Q&A

可以自由提問，關於會費、紙飛機活動、招新及競賽相關等皆可。 現場提問，現場回答。

English rendering.

Q&A.

You may ask anything you like — about membership dues, the paper plane activity, recruitment, the competition, and so on. Questions on the spot, answers on the spot.

The scope of the open questions

The four kinds of question listed on this slide — dues, the paper plane activity, recruitment, the competition — correspond one to one with the assembly's four main sections, which shows that a question slot was planned for from the start.

Opening assembly speaker's script contains no spoken script for the Q&A slot, which suggests the slot was answered off the cuff, with no text surviving.

items.title: Slide 12 · 收束 (Closing)
items.text:
感謝聆聽 ASJ英東物理社，啟動！

Thank you for listening to the ASJ Yingdong Physics Club. Let's start!

“啟動”

The last page closes with “啟動” (launch) rather than “end”, matching the opening script's line “today is only the beginning”.

items.title: 04.27 Assembly · Page-by-page record
items.text:
SLIDES 1–14 · 2026.04.27

What this page is

This page transcribes all 14 pages of 27 April assembly deck, page by page. The original is in Traditional Chinese and quotations are transcribed into simplified characters. The material between slides is added by this site, and the English renderings are added by this site as well.

The deck has two subjects: changes to the paper plane challenge (slides 1–3) and the membership dues and contribution credit system (slides 6–14).

items.title: Slide 1 · 三项变更 (Three changes)
items.text:
紙飛機挑戰賽活動說明

  1. 時間變動：改為 15.20–16.20
  2. 報名通道更改
  3. 現場佈局及流程介紹

English rendering.

Paper plane challenge — activity notes.

  1. Time change: moved to 15.20–16.20
  2. Registration channel changed
  3. On-site layout and run-through

This is the third version of the times

The 4.21 final version says 14:00–16:30; this slide changes it to 15:20–16:20; the poster draft says 15:00–16:10; the run-of-show document schedules the activity across a whole day.

The title of this slide uses the word “變動” (change), which makes this an active adjustment rather than a new plan.

items.title: Slide 2 · 場地地圖 (Venue map)
items.text:
紙飛機挑戰賽場地圖

English rendering.

Paper plane challenge venue map.

The venue map marks four surrounding buildings and three competition areas:

Category Labels Surrounding buildings Canteen · Gymnasium · Teaching building · Dormitory Competition areas Preparation area · Flight area · Start point

測量須知 以起點和紙飛機落點之間的直線距離為最終成績

English rendering.

How the measurement is done: the final result is the straight-line distance between the start point and where the paper plane lands.

How the measure of a result was settled

This is the clearest definition of how results were measured anywhere in the surviving material. The same measure is echoed in Flight festival promotion script (“precise recording with laser ranging equipment”) and in the run-of-show document (a laser ranging post); together the three explain why a laser rangefinder had to be bought rather than using a tape measure.

The vector original of the venue map is in Competition venue map.

items.title: Slide 3 · 疊法展示 (Folding demonstration)
items.text:
紙飛機疊法展示 現場将会有演示提供

English rendering.

Paper plane folding demonstration. A demonstration will be provided on site.

Where the “six folding methods” come from

This slide says only that “a demonstration will be provided” and gives no number. The figure of “6 種紙飛機折法” (six paper plane folding methods) comes from Flight festival promotion script and from A4 Flight Festival runbook (the teaching specialist post). This slide can be read as a preparatory note for that arrangement.

items.title: Slide 4 · 自媒體部門競選流程說明 (How the social media department election runs)
items.text:
自媒體部門競選流程說明

我們更看重的是：你是否願意認真做一件事，是否願意在團隊裏承擔責任， 是否願意把自己的興趣，變成真正的能力。

讓熱愛被看見 · 讓內容產生價值 · 讓社團擁有自己的未來

English rendering.

How the social media department election runs.

What we value more is: whether you are willing to do something seriously, whether you are willing to take on responsibilities within the team, and whether you are willing to turn your interests into real abilities.

Let what we love be seen · let the content have value · let the club have a future of its own.

From “notes” to “election”

The 4.21 assembly was the social media department's founding statement; the title of this slide has become “競選流程說明” (notes on the election process), which shows that the department had entered actual recruitment.

The wording on this slide is exactly the same as the English paragraph on slide 9 of 4.21, but the four items — recruiting areas / how it runs / what the department aims at / where it applies — are gone, leaving only the statement of values.

items.title: Slide 5 · 積分系統簡介 (Introduction to the points system)
items.text:
物理社積分系統简介

物理社積分系統記錄成員參與實驗、活動、分享和競賽的表現， 積分可兌換獎勵，激勵大家積極探索物理奧秘。

English rendering.

Introduction to the club's points system.

The club's points system records how members perform in experiments, activities, sharing sessions and competitions; points can be exchanged for rewards, encouraging everyone to explore the mysteries of physics.

Feature Notes Self-service Supports self-managed accounts Always on Open for login 7×24

The wording of this slide conflicts with slide 9

This slide says credits “可兌換獎勵” (can be exchanged for rewards), while slide 9, “The position of contribution credits”, explicitly lists what credits should not be taken for.

The two slides are four pages apart and their force is entirely different. This site keeps them side by side and does not judge which page represents the final position. See The merit system.

items.title: Slide 6 · 制度說明首頁 (Opening page of the system)
items.text:
物理社社費與貢獻積分制度說明 社費 · 貢獻積分 · 公開監督 · 合規邊界

English rendering.

The club's membership dues and contribution credit system. Dues · contribution credits · public oversight · compliance boundaries.

核心立場 - 讓社團活動更穩定 - 讓資金和規則更透明 - 讓制度邊界更清晰

English rendering.

Core position

  • Make club activities more stable
  • Make funding and rules more transparent
  • Make the boundaries of the system clearer

Four principles:

Principle Notes Public and transparent Income sources, uses of spending, receipts and balance all open to inspection Voluntary participation Paying dues is not a precondition for joining the club Compliant operation Dues and credits stay within bounds; no design that turns them into currency Club self-governance Supervised by the club's own treasurer and cashier, with the rules published in advance

依據：社費草案、法律條文與定義、穩定／代幣風險建議文檔

English rendering.

Basis: the dues draft, the legal provisions and definitions, and the document on stablecoin／token risk.

The three documents listed under “basis”

This slide names the three documents the system's design rests on: the dues draft, the legal provisions and definitions, and the document advising on stablecoin／token risk.

These are Merit rules draft, Legal provisions and definitions and Stability · discussion notes in 资料/. In line with the scope published in White papers and the retention boundary, this site does not publish their contents.

items.title: Slide 7 · 為什麼需要這套制度 (Why this system is needed)
items.text:
為什麼需要這套制度

制度不是為了「收費」，而是為了解決社團活動運行中的現實問題。

English rendering.

Why this system is needed.

The system is not there to “charge money”, but to solve the practical problems in running club activities.

# Problem How it shows up 1 The gap in reimbursement Formal approval and reimbursement at the school take time; equipment and materials often have to be bought in advance; the club needs the ability to cover costs for a short while 2 Varied activity spending Experiments, competitions, regular meetings and welfare activities all cost money; some spending may fall outside unified reimbursement; the purpose of each sum has to be kept clear 3 Trust and rules If the rules for dues and credits are unclear they invite misunderstanding; opaque accounts cause a crisis of trust; setting the rules in advance reduces disputes

用制度化方式保障活動持續開展，而不是用臨時辦法解決每一次支出。

English rendering.

The aim is to keep activities going by institutional means, not to solve every payment with an ad hoc measure.

How this page argues its case

This slide argues for the system with one structure: “three practical problems → one conclusion by contrast”. The most concrete item is “the gap in reimbursement / the ability to cover costs for a short while”: it explains why the club needed to hold cash, not merely keep accounts.

items.title: Slide 8 · 社費資金池設計 (Design of the dues fund pools)
items.text:
社費資金池設計 將經費用途分清楚，是後續公開監督和風險控制的基礎。

English rendering.

Design of the dues fund pools. Keeping the uses of the funds clearly separated is the basis for later public oversight and risk control.

Fixed fund pool

  • Used to cover reimbursable club spending in the meantime
  • Helps bridge the time gap before the school approves
  • Emphasis on keeping receipts and on later settlement
  • Should not be designed as a source of personal income

Activity fund pool

  • Used to cover part of the non-reimbursable activity costs
  • Such as small materials, organising activities and welfare arrangements
  • Spending should be directly related to club activities
  • Amounts, uses and the approval process must be public

建議原則：社費自願、用途明確、憑證齊全、定期公示。

English rendering.

Proposed principles: dues voluntary, uses clear, receipts complete, published regularly.

The naming difference between “活動資金池” and “流動資金池”

The second pool on this slide is called “活動資金池” (activity fund pool), while 物理社功勋系统资金流转白皮书 and 会员公开白皮书 call it “流動資金池” (circulating fund pool), defined there as “the part that enters a member's personal account and can be used for activities and resources inside the club”.

The two describe similar duties without being identical: this slide stresses “non-reimbursable costs”, the white papers stress “credited to the personal account”. Both are kept side by side.

items.title: Slide 9 · 貢獻積分的定位 (The position of contribution credits)
items.text:
貢獻積分的定位 積分可以記錄貢獻，但絕不能被包裝成貨幣、投資或收益憑證。

English rendering.

The position of contribution credits. Credits can record contribution, but must never be packaged as currency, an investment or a certificate of return.

What it should be What it should not be ✓ A record of contribution inside the club ✕ Currency, a token or a coin ✓ A tool for encouraging participation ✕ An investment or financing instrument ✓ A record of entitlement to welfare activities ✕ A promise of fixed returns or dividends ✓ A supporting mechanism for club self-governance ✕ A certificate that can be transferred, traded or cashed out

This slide sets the compliance floor of the whole system

The wording of the four items on the right (“must never be packaged as”) is the strongest language in the whole deck. It separates credits from three things — currency, investment, certificates of return — and corresponds to the analysis of the “four characteristics” of token financing and illegal fundraising in Legal provisions and definitions.

items.title: Slide 10 · 積分如何獲得與使用 (How credits are earned and used)
items.text:
積分如何獲得與使用 積分應圍繞真實貢獻產生，規則必須提前公佈。

English rendering.

How credits are earned and used. Credits should arise from real contribution, and the rules must be published in advance.

Source Examples Participation Attending regular meetings, taking part in experiments, joining club activities Contribution Explaining problems, helping to organise, completing club tasks Performance Winning a competition, standing out at a large event Record Forming contribution credits under published rules

使用邊界 - 僅限社團內部福利活動或權益記錄 - 不得轉讓、交易、折現或承諾經濟回報 - 不得用積分製造「投入越多收益越高」的預期

English rendering.

Boundaries on use

  • Confined to welfare activities inside the club, or to records of entitlement
  • May not be transferred, traded, cashed out or promised as a financial return
  • May not be used to create the expectation that “the more you put in, the higher the return”

“不得製造預期” (may not create expectations)

The third boundary is the most unusual on this slide: what it restricts is not an act but the formation of an expectation. Logically it complements slide 9's “not an investment instrument”.

items.title: Slide 11 · 爭議處理機制 (How disputes are handled)
items.text:
爭議處理機制 規則越清晰，越能保護社員、社團幹部和指導老師。

English rendering.

How disputes are handled. The clearer the rules, the better they protect members, club officers and the supervising teacher.

Four steps:

Step Action 1 Submit an application The member applies in writing and gives the reason 2 Review and record Review under the rules, keeping the date, the amount and the basis 3 Report the outcome Tell the member the outcome, and publish the rule relied on if necessary 4 Appeal and explain Members may object, add further explanation or ask for a review

Damage to equipment

  • Should be handled on the basis of facts, evidence and the clauses of the constitution
  • Simply deducting credits is not recommended as a substitute for formal compensation
  • Room should be left for explanation, negotiation and appeal

Avoiding overbearing clauses

  • Reduce one-sided statements such as “the club holds the final right of interpretation”
  • Replace them with “interpretation according to the constitution, open to oversight and appeal”
  • Outcomes should be traceable and explainable

One point on this slide worth singling out

The section on avoiding overbearing clauses actively limits the club's own power, and asks for “interpretation according to the constitution, open to oversight and appeal” in place of “the club holds the final right of interpretation”. That is not common in the governing documents of student clubs.

items.title: Slide 12 · 公開帳本與知情權 (The public ledger and the right to know)
items.text:
公開帳本與知情權 透明不是負擔，而是減少誤會和保護社團幹部的機制。

English rendering.

The public ledger and the right to know. Transparency is not a burden but a mechanism that reduces misunderstanding and protects club officers.

Layer Content The public ledger Receipts · flows · balance Overall income and spending Income sources published; uses of spending published; summarised and published regularly Personal records One's own dues record; one's own credit record Original receipts Screenshots of payment; invoices or receipts; purchasing lists Oversight mechanisms Members may ask; teachers advise; problems may be appealed

Transparency argued as a protection for officers

The subtitle defines transparency as a mechanism that protects club officers, not merely one that restrains them. That view differs from the usual “transparency is for oversight”.

items.title: Slide 13 · 執行落地流程 (Putting the system into practice)
items.text:
執行落地流程 建議先試行、再修訂，避免制度一開始就過重或過急。

English rendering.

Putting the system into practice. The suggestion is to try it first and revise afterwards, so that the system is not too heavy or too hasty from the start.

Step Action 1 Publish the draft Explain the purpose of the system to members and teachers and gather opinions in one place 2 Revise the detailed rules Make the rules for dues, credits, oversight and dispute handling explicit 3 Set up the ledger Record income and spending, receipts, personal records and the publication cycle in one place 4 Review regularly Check how it works each month or each term and revise what does not

“先試行、再修訂” (try it first, revise afterwards)

This slide makes clear that the system was not written once and left as it was, but that the mechanism of revision is built into the process itself (step 4). That matches the later multi-version evolution of the merit system — v1.0 → the first official version → the member-public version.

items.title: Slide 14 · 收束 (Closing)
items.text:
讓制度服務社團建設

每一筆錢都花在明處， 每一份貢獻都被公平記錄。

English rendering.

Let the system serve the building of the club.

Every sum of money is spent in the open, every contribution is recorded fairly.

The end answering the beginning

The two lines of the last page answer respectively to public and transparent among the four principles on slide 6 (money spent in the open) and to the position of credits on slides 9–10 (contribution recorded, but not turned into currency).

items.title: A4 Paper Flight Festival · Event Overview
items.text:
03 / THE MEMORY COLLECTION · THE FLIGHT PROJECT

Sources

Compiled from 21 April assembly deck (final) (page 6), 27 April assembly deck, Flight festival promotion script, A4 Flight Festival runbook and Paper plane purchase list.

items.title: The nature of the event
items.text:
The event was not an origami activity alone. It put physics, engineering, competition and creativity on the same field: registration, test flights, laser ranging, live projection, the awards, the record — all of it organised and carried through by the student club itself.

Paper for sails, a flight path over Yingdong.

items.title: Basic information
items.text:
Item Details Time 30 April 2026 (four conflicting versions exist, see below) Venue The school's main sports field (the run of show sets a separate morning session: indoor gymnasium) Participants All students and teachers of every section of the school Registration By group, the registration channel opens on site Scoring basis The straight-line distance between the start point and where the paper plane lands is the final result

Both the time and the group size have several versions

Time: the 4.21 assembly final deck and the publicity draft say 14:00–16:30; the 4.27 assembly changes it to 15:20–16:20; the original poster artwork says 15:00–16:10; the run of show document says all day (gymnasium in the morning + main sports field in the afternoon).

Group size: the publicity draft says 2–6 people; the sign-in sheet says 4–6 people; the run of show says “groups of at most six, prizes awarded by group”.

This site keeps them side by side and does not merge them into one “correct” version. The full comparison is in Sources.

items.title: The three moments in the original plan
items.text:
The run of show document split the event into three parts: fold → measure → challenge:

  1. Fold · starting from a single crease The plan set up folding instruction and free flight, so that participants first worked with their hands and then observed how each test flight differed.
  2. Measure · turning the flight path into data The notes from the 4.27 assembly defined the result as the straight-line distance between the start point and where the paper plane landed, and divided the site into a preparation area and a flight area.
  3. Challenge · improving through one attempt after another The competition format set out a preliminary flight, the official flight, a final for the top eight, and the student–teacher challenge.

items.title: Site layout
items.text:
The site map from the 4.27 assembly marks the preparation area, the flight area and the start point; the run of show document instead set up a free flight area, a distance challenge area and a creative display area, run zone by zone.

The boundary was marked out with isolation posts and warning tape (5 cm × 46 m); the entrance, the start baseline, the test-flight area and the direction of the toilets were each indicated by one of 7 guide signs.

  • Site layout map
  • The original guide signs are in the Design Archive
  • Vector original Competition venue map

items.title: Awards
items.text:
Award Places How it is decided Competition Core Award · Champion 1 By distance flown in the official competition Competition Core Award · Runner-up 2 By distance flown in the official competition Competition Core Award · Third place 3 By distance flown in the official competition School record holder 1 The longest flight of this event Best Creative Paper Plane Award First 1 / Second 3 / Third 5 School-wide vote + judges Student–Teacher Interaction Popularity Award 3 The student group with the most interaction and the highest popularity in the student–teacher challenge Prediction Lucky Prize 30 / unlimited Drawn at random from those who predicted correctly Outstanding Volunteer Award Several Selected from the staff

The morning achievement award has no quota: reaching any of the 10 m / 20 m / 30 m challenge lines in the distance challenge area earned it on the spot.

items.text:

items.title: Teaching: 6 folding patterns
items.text:
The teaching corner was staffed by club members throughout (the run of show names 胡益成、肖子扬 as teaching specialists), demonstrating 6 high-performance paper plane folding patterns on site and handing out the diagrams.

From basic structure to flight optimisation, so that everyone can pick it up quickly.

items.title: Curatorial intent
items.text:
The ranking was decided by flight distance. The spoken script stressed three further points:

Whose design has the most ideas, who is best at solving problems with physics thinking, who can take a simple paper plane and really give it a bit of a technological feel.

Because where the launch velocity comes from, how energy is converted during the flight, how the wing shape and the position of the centre of gravity together decide how it performs — these questions are physics in themselves.

items.title: About the results
items.text:
This site publishes no results

The surviving material records the preparation only. The three on-site forms (registration sheet, sign-in sheet, results sheet) are all blank templates, with no entries at all. This site therefore does not fill in placings, distance results or a “school record” figure.

→ For the full plan and the assignment of roles, see Run of Show → For the story of the day itself, see A4 Paper Flight Festival

Item Unit price Quantity Subtotal Purpose Laser rangefinder 500m ¥159 1 ¥159 Measuring paper plane results Whiteboard writing board ¥20 1 ¥20 Recording results Warning tape 5 cm × 46 m ¥17.8 2 ¥35.6 Dividing the areas Custom signature board 2.3 m × 3.5 m ¥158 1 ¥158 Signatures — ¥372.6 Total

A few notes on this list

  • In the “venue” column, the whiteboard is marked “main sports field & later use”, which indicates that the item was planned as a reusable asset rather than a one-off material;
  • The “product link” column contains both Taobao links and Xianyu mini-program links, which indicates that the purchasing channels were not uniform;
  • The total of ¥372.6 was added up by this site from the subtotals in the list; the original list has no total row.

items.title: Two key pieces of equipment
items.text:
Rangefinder spec

500 m range · ¥159 · one unit purchased

Laser rangefinder (500 m, ¥159) — the highest unit price in the list, and the only one with a single purpose. Its presence corresponds directly to the scoring basis established at the 04.27 assembly:

taking the straight-line distance between the start point and where the paper plane lands as the final result

A straight-line distance calls for a measurement that can be reproduced and re-checked when disputed; that is why laser ranging was used rather than a tape measure.

Custom signature board (2.3 m × 3.5 m, ¥158) — an area of about 8.05 m2, the only item on the list that had to be custom-made, and second only to the rangefinder in unit price.

items.title: Run of Show
items.text:
THE RUNBOOK · FROM PREPARATION TO WRAP-UP

Sources

This page is compiled from A4 Flight Festival runbook, the most complete execution plan among the surviving material: the rhythm of four preparation weeks, the hour-by-hour arrangements of the morning and afternoon sessions, the posts and responsibilities of all staff across five dedicated groups, the awards and the materials list. See also Flight festival role assignments (an abbreviated division of labour and a second competition format) and Runbook (another version).

items.title: Basic information
items.text:
Item Details Event time 2026, month X day X (all day; the date was left blank and undecided in the original document) Venue Morning: indoor gymnasium · Afternoon: the school's main sports field Participants All students and teachers of every section of the school Overall lead 孔耀聪 Executive vice-president 孙弘毅

Why this page says “month X, day X”

The date field of the original run of show document is left blank. The other surviving material gives four mutually conflicting dates and time slots; this site keeps them side by side and does not merge them into one “correct” time. See Sources · Conflicting time statements.

items.title: Preparation period (3 weeks to 1 day before the event)
items.text:
About the checkboxes

The preparation period is a to-do schedule in the original document, so this site presents it as a checklist. Every box is empty — the original never moved past the planning stage, and no item records having been carried out.

items.title: 3 weeks before
items.text:
• The overall lead finalises the final event plan and the overall budget, and completes school approval and the venue / equipment applications
  • The coordination group compiles the full-process event document, clarifies the division of labour between the groups, and collects competition registration information

items.title: 2 weeks before
items.text:
• The logistics group gathers material requirements, compiles the purchasing list and gets it approved
  • The publicity and filming group produces the warm-up poster, the folding diagrams, the check-in wall and the warm-up post, and publishes them through the school's channels
  • The competition operations and design group draws up the competition rules / scoring criteria, sets up the registration channel and answers competitors' questions

items.title: 1 week before (Monday)
items.text:
• The overall lead completes the invitations and liaison for 3 principals and the participating teachers
  • The competition operations and design group collects registration information, completes the grouping of competitors and produces the schedule / score sheet / competitor numbers
  • The competition operations and design group runs pre-duty training for referees, distance measurers and recorders
  • The logistics group completes all material purchasing, sets up a ledger and keeps everything classified

items.title: 1 day before
items.text:
• The logistics group + the on-site execution group complete the zoning and marking of the venue and test equipment such as the laser rangefinder
  • The overall lead + the vice-president organise all staff for a full run-through, simulating how emergencies would be handled
  • Each group holds an internal meeting to reconfirm the next day's post duties and requirements
  • The logistics group distributes all materials to their places and completes the final count

items.title: 08:00–08:40 All staff on post and ready
items.text:
1. Each group leader confirms that staff are on post, materials are in place and equipment is working
  2. Key equipment and materials such as the laser rangefinder and the check-in wall are tested a second time
  3. The emergency arrangements for each post are reconfirmed

items.title: 09:00–10:30 Folding and free flight for everyone
items.text:
1. The on-site execution group opens the signature and check-in area and guides students and teachers to sign, take photos and stick up wish notes
  2. 胡益成、肖子扬 are on post at the teaching corner, teaching 6 paper plane folding patterns hand over hand and handing out the diagrams
  3. The on-site execution group assigns posts to keep order in the free flight area, the distance challenge area and the creative display area
  4. For students who reach the standard in the distance challenge area, the logistics group hands out the achievement award on the spot
  5. The publicity and filming group films throughout, editing short videos in real time and posting them to the school's channels
  6. The logistics group patrols the whole site, topping up A4 paper, prizes, stationery and other materials in good time
  7. The logistics group deals quickly with temporary equipment failures on site
  8. The overall lead + the vice-president patrol the whole site, coordinating emergencies and receiving the guests who arrive
  9. The overall lead + the vice-president get students and teachers interacting and set the mood of the event

items.title: 10:30–11:30 Engineering group showcase and testing
items.text:
1. The competition operations and design group: 1 person hosts, 2 people take charge of judging + distance measurement, 1 person records and posts the results
  2. 1 person in the competition operations and design group hands out prizes and 3 people keep order on site
  3. The on-site execution group: 3 people guide students to watch in an orderly way and explain the test rules at the same time
  4. The publicity and filming group films the highlights of the testing, records each team's results and prepares material for the afternoon's opening video

items.title: 11:30–12:00 School-wide prediction contest
items.text:
1. The on-site execution group hands out and collects the prediction tickets
  2. The on-site execution group seals the collected prediction tickets in the ballot box
  3. The coordination group posts the prediction draw rules and the draw time on site
  4. The coordination group guides students to take part in the prediction in an orderly way and answers their questions

items.title: 12:00–12:30 Morning wrap-up + short debrief
items.text:
1. The logistics group collects the materials from each area, counts the remaining supplies and tidies the venue briefly
  2. The competition operations and design group sorts out the morning's test results and confirms that the afternoon's competitors will be present
  3. The publicity and filming group sorts the morning's footage and finishes editing the afternoon opening recap video
  4. The overall lead + the vice-president gather the core team for a short 10-minute debrief
  5. In response to the morning's problems, the afternoon's arrangements and staffing are adjusted immediately

items.title: Event day · Afternoon session (main sports field 13:30–16:00)
12:30–14:00 Final preparation before the competition
items.text:
1. All staff are on post, and each group leader confirms materials, equipment and the state of the venue
  2. The on-site execution group finishes setting up the isolation tape in the flight area on the sports field, dividing it into two flight fields

items.title: 14:20–15:20 Official flight competition
items.text:

items.text: 01 / THE MEMORY COLLECTION · OUR STORY

items.title: Curiosity came first, and then our story
items.text: Not just a name on a list of activities. It was a place where understanding, expression and practice could happen.

items.title: The club's original intent: approaching physics in our own way
items.text:
Material from the assembly of 21 April 2026 describes the club this way: it was founded to give students a platform to understand physics, express physics and practise physics.

The opening script divided the club's direction into two lines:

  1. Make physics interesting, tangible and open to participation — experiments, activities, challenges;
  2. Let students who want to go deeper go further — competition problem walkthroughs and thinking training.

Experiments, project design, photography, editing, copywriting and event organising could all be ways of taking part.

items.title: Egg Drop
items.text:
THE FIRST EXPERIMENT

What this page rests on

Recruitment talk script lists “Egg Drop” among the physics club's activities of the past year, and states its significance as “a test of hands-on ability, and still more a display of engineering thinking and physical modelling ability”.

But the surviving material contains no separate plan, date, rules or record of results for this activity; this recruitment script is the only thing that mentions it. This page therefore gives no date and reports no outcome, and the description of the physics problem below is a general account of this kind of challenge, not what was said on the day.

items.title: The first thing we did
items.text:
Drop an egg from a height, and have it come down intact.

It sounds like a joke, but it is a complete engineering problem: spread the impact force out over time and space, trade structural deformation for a lower peak stress, stretch out the transfer of momentum with a cushioning layer. What is fragile is not the egg; a structure without design is.

items.title: What this kind of challenge examines
items.text:
• How the impulse at the moment of landing can be absorbed by the structure rather than by the shell
  • How the thickness, stiffness and arrangement of the cushioning material affect the peak stress
  • How the position of the centre of mass affects the landing attitude: once the attitude is offset, everything calculated before it is void

items.title: What the recruitment script says
items.text:
Through structural design and shock absorption, the students let an egg that looks fragile “survive” a fall from a height; the process is not only a test of hands-on ability, but a display of engineering thinking and physical modelling ability.

—— Recruitment talk script

items.title: Why it was repeatedly cited
items.text:
The activity later became the first story told in the club's recruitment presentations — because it answers “what does this club actually do” most directly:

Physics is not formulas on paper; it happens in the hands, before the eyes, and in the five minutes after a failure when you build it again.

items.title: A4 Paper Flight Festival
items.text:
2026.04.30 · PREPARATION ARCHIVE

First, what kind of material this is

The surviving material records preparation, not results.

  • The three on-site forms (报名表 registration form, 签到表 sign-in sheet, 成绩表 results sheet) are all blank templates, with nothing actually filled in;
  • this site therefore publishes no placing, no distance result and no “campus record” figure.

The activity's time, format and some arrangements exist in several versions across the material; this site keeps them side by side, see Sources · Conflicting statements of time.

items.title: The nature of the event
items.text:
The event was not an origami activity alone. It put physics, engineering, competition and invention onto the same patch of ground: registration, trial flights, laser ranging, live projection, awards, a record attempt, all organised and carried through by the student club itself.

The assembly publicity script put it this way:

You can be a competitor, you can be a designer, you can even be simply an observer — but whatever your role, you will see how an ordinary sheet of A4 paper flies an extreme distance under the combined effect of structure, aerodynamics and technique.

items.title: Competition procedure
items.text:
Version A — source: A4 Flight Festival runbook

  • Group stage: 1 trial flight + 3 official flights; the best score selects the last 8
  • Final of the last 8: 5 flights; added to the group stage score and taking the best, deciding first, second and third place and the holder of the campus record
  • Student–teacher challenge: student groups arranged their own match against teachers, teachers could use the physics club's equipment, and an award was given win or lose

Version B — source: Flight festival role assignments

  • Group stage: 1 trial flight + 2 official flights; the best score selects the last 8
  • Final of the last 8: 3 flights; added to the group stage score and taking the best

The two versions disagree on the number of flights; they are not merged here.

items.title: Registration
items.text:
Stated rule Source Register as a group, 2–6 people per group, with a registration desk open on the day Flight festival promotion script 4–6 people per group 紙飛機挑戰賽 签到表.docx (file name in traditional characters) At most six people per group, awards given by group A4 Flight Festival runbook

The scoring rule was consistent: the final result is the straight-line distance between the start point and where the paper plane lands (27 April assembly deck, page 2, “Measurement notes”).

items.title: How results were verified on site
items.text:
This was the most technical part of the whole event:

Role Duty Chief judge (sink) Interpreting the rules, deciding whether a flight was valid, final ruling on disputes Check-in Checking competitors in and keeping order, keeping unauthorised people out of the flight area Ranging Recording flight data precisely with a laser rangefinder (500 m range) Scoring Live projection of the standings, so that everything was open and clear Recording Results noted on a whiteboard, and after the event made into a public list and a record board

Laser ranging was chosen over a tape measure because the rule of “straight-line distance” calls for a measurement that can be reproduced and re-checked when it is disputed.

items.title: What survived from that day
items.text:
The value of an event is not only in the day itself. The wrap-up plan also included:

  • Publishing a recap post and a short video within 24 hours, filing the material by category, and submitting a report reviewing how the content performed
  • Publishing the final list of winners and the campus record within 3 days, and making and putting up the campus record board
  • Counting the remaining materials into storage, checking the funds, and submitting the reimbursement documents

items.title: 2 · The Paper Plane Flight Festival
items.text:
The paper plane activity of the science and technology festival was formally announced. The spoken script deliberately corrected a common misunderstanding:

It is not a game of “fold it anyhow and throw it”. It can itself become a very good physics inquiry activity.

What the script pointed to was this question: where the initial velocity of the flight comes from, how energy is transformed during the flight, and how factors such as wing shape, the position of the centre of mass and air resistance affect how it performs.

What we hope everyone finally sees is not only “who flew the furthest”, but: whose design had the most thought in it, who solved the problem best with physical thinking, and who could give a simple paper plane a genuine touch of engineering.

→ The activity plan is in the Flight Project and the Run of Show

items.text:
You do not need to be “very good” from the start, and you do not need to have learned a lot of material beyond the syllabus. What really matters is whether you are willing to stay curious, whether you are willing to ask a “why”, and whether you are willing to find the uncommon rules in a world that looks ordinary.

During recruitment a “Physics Club Recruitment Interest Questionnaire” was also handed out, asking about the acceptable range for club dues (50 / 100 / 200 yuan or other), skills and role preferences (editing, photography, both, none for now), and whether students were willing to take part in content production for pay.

items.title: Training approach
items.text:
Not “handing out answers”, but taking problems apart, building models, and training a way of thinking in physics. The club's two lines were pursued in parallel:

  1. Make physics interesting, tangible and open to participation — experiments, activities, challenges
  2. Let students who want to go deeper go further — competition problem walkthroughs and thinking training

The recruitment script puts this line this way:

Here it is not about “handing out answers”, but about taking problems apart, building models and training a real way of thinking in physics, so that students can move from “able to solve problems” to “able to think”.

items.text:
From basic mechanics apparatus to extended inquiry equipment, from competition simulation tools to an innovative experiment platform, we tried to give every member real, workable experimental conditions, so that physics no longer stays on paper but happens in the hands and before the eyes.

—— Recruitment talk script

items.title: Suspension
items.text:
THE LAST FRAME

This page rests on something different from the rest

Every other page of this site rests on originals in 资料/; this page does not.

  • Among all the files in 资料/, not one contains the words “suspension”, “termination”, “disbandment” or “end”;
  • so when and why the club ended cannot be confirmed from the surviving material;
  • the only basis is the commissioning note for the memorial site, which gives the date of suspension as 29 May 2026.

This site records it on that basis, and marks clearly that its level of sourcing differs from the other pages.

items.title: The last date that survives
items.text:
The content file with the latest modification time in the material directory is the file 演示文稿1.pptx of 12 May 2026 (the assembly at which the four groups and the merit system appeared).

File Last modified 演示文稿1.pptx 2026-05-12 20:05 第一版设计饮料杯.svg 2026-05-07 19:36 batch_页面 1–2.png 2026-05-07 19:26 27 April assembly deck 2026-04-27 13:47

The surviving material ends at 12 May. After that there is no record of any new activity, assembly or purchase.

items.title: There was no closing ceremony
items.text: There was no closing ceremony, no final event, and no formal farewell script. It was simply that from that day on, assemblies were no longer scheduled, competitions no longer took entries, the purchasing list stopped gaining rows, and club badges stopped reaching new members' hands.

items.title: We chose to record it as it was
items.text:
This site does not narrate the suspension as a drama. It is simply an ordinary fact: a group of people made some things together over a stretch of time, and then that stretch of time ended.

In the 27 April version of the assembly slides, the time of the paper plane challenge had just been changed to 15:20–16:20; the 21 April recruitment questionnaire was still asking students “can you accept a 50-yuan club fee”; in the 12 May slides the four groups had just been divided, and the demo video for the merit system had just been finished. All of it is still here, nothing cleared away.

items.title: On sourcing
items.text:
Both pages are based on the original files in the 资料/ directory and use no second-hand retelling.

The merit system needs a word of explanation: it was an organisational experiment. The surviving material includes the full rules, the record model and a glossary, and also parts that never landed. This site preserves that material as it stands, keeps its boundary notes, and does not decide on the reader's behalf which parts were carried out.

On rosters and records

Rosters and ledgers are primary data: names, amounts and dates are transcribed from the originals, without alteration or summary. For how personal information was weighed, see Thanks · Editorial notes.

items.title: Governance & Roster
items.text:
GOVERNANCE · RULES, OFFICERS & ROSTERS

A club needs more than activities; it also needs rules and a division of labour. This part gathers two things: how money is collected, spent and recorded, and who holds which position and belongs to which group.

Both pages take the originals in the 资料/ directory as their authority:

  • Membership Dues and Contribution Credits — the club dues and contribution-credit rules set out in full at the 27 April 2026 assembly
  • Organisational Structure and Roster — 14 officers, four groups, and the list of advisors

A note on conventions

The original CSVs and slide decks are in traditional Chinese characters; this site gives the whole page in the conventional simplified forms, quotations and personal and group names included. Where the pages find contradictions in the material (dates, amounts, headcounts), they keep the versions side by side and neither merge them nor draw inferences.

items.title: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System
items.text:
Sources

This page is compiled from 27 April assembly deck pages 6–14 (the explanation of the club dues and contribution credit system) and Notes on how dues were used. The former is the system design; the latter is the explanation of costs aimed at students. See also Recruitment survey (intentions regarding club dues).
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Position
items.text:
The system is not there to “collect money”, but to solve real problems in the running of club activities. At the assembly on 27 April 2026, the physics club laid out the rules on club dues and credits in full:

  • Open and transparent —— sources of income, uses of expenditure, vouchers and balances are all open to inspection
  • Voluntary participation —— paying dues is not a precondition for joining the club; not paying does not affect participation in everyday activities
  • Compliant operation —— club dues and credits stay within their bounds and are not designed as a currency
  • Club self-governance —— supervised by the club's own treasurer and cashier, with the rules published in advance

Supporting documents: “Draft Club Dues”, “Legal Clauses and Definitions”, “Stablecoin / Token Risk Advisory Document”.
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Why this system is needed
items.text: Practical problem How it shows up The reimbursement lag Official school approval and reimbursement take a process, while equipment and materials often have to be bought in advance, so the club must be able to cover costs in the short term Varied activity spending Experiments, competitions, regular meetings and welfare activities all generate costs, and some spending falls outside unified reimbursement, so the purpose of funds must be clearly distinguished Trust and rules Club dues and credits invite misunderstanding when the rules are unclear; an opaque ledger creates a crisis of trust; setting the rules early reduces disputes
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Fund pool design
items.text:
The funds are split into two pools with clear purposes, which is the basis for later public oversight and risk control.

Fixed fund pool —— used to advance club spending that can be reimbursed, covering the lag before school approval. Emphasis on keeping vouchers and settling them afterwards; it is not a source of personal gain.

Activity fund pool —— used to cover some activity costs that cannot be reimbursed, such as small materials, event organisation and welfare arrangements; spending must be directly related to club activities, and the amount, purpose and approval process are public.

Guiding principles: club dues voluntary, purposes clear, vouchers complete, disclosed regularly.
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Where contribution credits stand
items.text:
Credits record contribution, but they must never be packaged as a currency, an investment, or a certificate of return.

They should be: a record of contribution within the club · a tool to encourage participation · a record of entitlement to welfare activities · an auxiliary mechanism for club self-governance.

They should not be: a currency, token or coin · an investment or financing instrument · a promise of fixed return or dividends · a certificate that can be transferred, traded or cashed out.

Credits are earned around real contribution: participation (attending regular meetings, taking part in experiments, joining club activities), contribution (explaining problems, helping to organise, completing club tasks), performance (winning competitions, outstanding contribution to a major event), ultimately forming a record of contribution under public rules.

There is only one limit on their use: they are confined to welfare activities or records of entitlement within the club, they may not be transferred, traded, cashed out, or made to promise an economic return, and credits may not be used to create the expectation that “the more you put in, the more you get back”.
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Dispute handling mechanism
items.text:
The clearer the rules, the better they protect club members, club officers and supervising teachers.

  1. Submit a request —— a member submits a written request and explains the reason
  2. Review the record —— review according to the rules, keeping the time, amount and basis on file
  3. Return a result —— inform the member of the outcome and, where necessary, publish the basis in the rules
  4. Explain and appeal —— members may raise objections, add explanations, or apply for a review

Damage to equipment is handled on the basis of facts, evidence and the clauses of the constitution; a simple deduction of credits is not used in place of formal compensation, and room is kept for explanation, negotiation and appeal. At the same time the club actively avoids one-sided clauses such as “the club holds the final right of interpretation”, replacing them with “interpreted according to the constitution, open to oversight and appeal”.
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Public ledger and the right to know
items.text:
Transparency is not a burden; it is a mechanism for reducing misunderstanding and protecting club officers.

  • Overall income and expenditure: publish sources of income, publish uses of expenditure, summarise and disclose regularly
  • Personal records: one's own dues record, one's own credit record
  • Original vouchers: payment screenshots, invoices or receipts, purchasing lists
  • Oversight mechanism: member enquiries, teacher guidance, raising objections
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Putting it into practice
items.text:
1. Publish the draft —— explain the purpose of the system to members and teachers, and gather opinions
  2. Revise the detailed rules —— clarify the rules on dues, credits, oversight and dispute handling
  3. Establish the ledger —— record income and expenditure, vouchers, personal records and the disclosure cycle in one place
  4. Review regularly —— check how it is working every month or every term and revise what is wrong

Every sum of money is spent in the open, every contribution is recorded fairly.
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: Uses of the dues
items.text:
1. Enriching what the club does —— themed events, fun experiments, challenges, showcase activities
  2. Buying and building experimental equipment —— so that club activities do not stop at “listening” and “watching”
  3. Supporting distinctive projects and creative activities —— small science and engineering builds, fun competitions, aircraft / model activities
  4. Activity prizes and incentives —— awards for excellent participation, competition prizes, activity mementos
  5. Keeping the club running steadily over the long term —— so that more new activities can go ahead later
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: What recruitment asked about
items.text: At the recruitment stage the club used a questionnaire to learn what people actually intended, rather than assuming everyone was willing to pay: the range of dues they would accept (50 / 100 / 200 yuan or another amount), their skills and preferred roles (editing, photography, both, or none for now), whether they were willing to take part in content production for payment, and their reasons for wanting to join the physics club. The results of the questionnaire are used only for the club's internal statistics and planning.
path: Membership Dues and the Contribution Credit System

items.title: The Merit System
items.text:
LATE STAGE · THE MERIT SYSTEM

Sources

This page is compiled from Merit system historical record and Member white paper.

The first is a compilation of historical material written specifically for this memorial site (compiled 18 September 2026), and it sets out explicitly the three-tier publication boundary this site should adopt.

The merit system was an internal mechanism that the Physics Club tried to establish in its late period for recording dues, activities, contributions and rewards. It began with the need for transparency in club dues, for activity accounting and for a record of member contributions, and later developed step by step into an electronic system comprising a fixed fund pool, a circulating fund pool, individual accounts, a public ledger and a reward pool.

In this system, members' payments, participation in activities, collection of materials, receipt of rewards and applications for refunds all leave a record. The system was not only for keeping accounts; it was there to make the club's operations visible and to leave a trace of those who took part actively.

Although the Physics Club has disbanded, the merit system remains an important organisational experiment in this history. It represents the serious attempt its members once made at transparency, fairness, rules and long-term operation.

—— Quoted from chapter 13, “Short text usable on the memorial site”, of that document, by permission of the original

items.title: Origins of the system
items.text:
The merit system appeared because of several concrete problems the Physics Club faced in actual operation:

  • How dues should be recorded clearly
  • How activity costs should be accounted for
  • How public funds should be made transparent
  • How members who took part actively should be seen
  • How rewards should be paid out
  • How members should be able to look up their own balance and history

The original idea was not simply to make a spreadsheet, but to establish a fairly complete internal record system: once a member paid their dues, the system formed a corresponding record; when the club spent money, ran activities, paid rewards or settled accounts, the system left the accounts alongside; and members could view their own account and the public ledger.

The core demands were three: transparency · traceability · sustainability.

items.title: Basic positioning
items.text:
In the final public wording, merit is positioned as the Physics Club's internal tool for recording dues and contributions, used to record members' payments, use in activities, public expenditure, reward payments and changes to accounts.

The boundary the system stressed repeatedly:

Merit is not currency

Merit is used only under the club's internal rules. It is not open to people outside the club, is not used as a payment instrument outside the club, and offers no free transfer between members, no buying and selling, no discounting to cash and no other form of external circulation.

This boundary was retained across several versions of the white paper, and is the compliance floor of the whole design.

items.title: The real problems it was meant to solve
items.text: Stage What the system did Payment Every entry leaves the amount, the time, the handler, the review status and a voucher Activity Income, cost, deductions and the balance form a project record Materials Collection and settlement can be checked, and any difference has somewhere to go Rewards Paid from the reward pool after multi-signature confirmation, with a stated reason and a review record Refunds Bound to account closure or withdrawal from the club; real funds flow out and the record is written off Lookup Members can view their own details and the club's public ledger

items.title: In the end it was more than a software project
items.text:
Seen from the standpoint of historical material, it shows a student club working through real problems: how to deal with opaque dues, how to account for activity costs, how public funds should be retained, how active members should be rewarded, how the system should avoid distortion, and how the accounting side should move from hand-kept books to audit oversight.

The most representative line from the release speech is:

The Physics Club is not only a place to do physics together; it should also become a club that is governed by rules, keeps a ledger, records contributions and has long-term vitality.
